staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, and the line locations below are grounded in this tree. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `34179b3354915f48134689f412e3a7eb363356a4`, but the prepared workspace used for the saved reproduction is the commit above.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42487630 (fmt): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzzer_named_arg [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42487630
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged 24-byte `fuzzer_named_arg` witness selects the `float` specialization, materializes `9.5f` from the first four data bytes, and supplies the format string `"{:.0e}"`. `write<float>()` therefore requests one significant digit in exponential form for a binary32 value. On the executed fallback path, `fallback_format()` rounds that single digit upward, propagates a carry into the leading position, and then mishandles the carry by writing `'0'` instead of `'1'` while incrementing the decimal exponent. The later non-fixed trailing-zero cleanup interprets that bogus leading `'0'` as a removable trailing zero, increments the exponent again, and shrinks the digits buffer to length 0. `float_writer::prettify()` still takes the exponential-format path, unconditionally reads `*digits_`, and calls `copy_str(digits_ + 1, digits_ + num_digits_, it)` with `num_digits_ == 0`, so `std::copy` walks forward off the end of the stack `memory_buffer` digits array. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting 1-byte stack-buffer-overflow read in `fmt::v7::detail::buffer<char>::push_back(char const&)` at `include/fmt/core.h:729`. The fix changes the carry-repair step to `buf[0] = '1';`, which preserves one digit (`"1e+01"`) and prevents the zero-length digits state.

source.description: First non-entrypoint project statement that materializes vulnerability-relevant data from attacker-controlled bytes. On the crashing witness, the selected `Item` type is `float`, so this copy creates the exact `9.5f` rounding edge case that later reaches `fallback_format()`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` begins with selector byte `0x1a`, so `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` dispatches to `invoke_fmt<float>` with `argsize = 1`. The next four bytes are `00 00 18 41`, which `assignFromBuf<float>` copies into `item` as little-endian IEEE754 `9.5f`.

sink.description: Closest project sink to the ASan crash. `copy_str()` consumes the invalid source range built by `float_writer::prettify()` when `num_digits_ == 0`, so `std::copy` reads sequential bytes from the stack `memory_buffer` until the iterator reaches the first byte past the object.
sink.note: ASan reports the trap in `fmt::v7::detail::buffer<char>::push_back(char const&)` at `include/fmt/core.h:729`, but the closest project-level read sink is this `copy_str()` wrapper around `std::copy`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. When rounding propagates a carry past the most significant generated digit, the fallback formatter increments the exponent but repairs the leading digit with `'0'` instead of `'1'`. For the staged `9.5f` / `"{:.0e}"` witness, that wrong `'0'` is later stripped away entirely, leaving a zero-digit buffer that the exponent-format writer cannot handle. The fix changes this exact assignment to `buf[0] = '1';`.

parser_admitted.description: At this call the harness has already selected the `float` specialization, copied the fuzz bytes into `item1`, and materialized the attacker-controlled format string. The remaining path is entirely inside fmt's floating-point formatting logic.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the point where the two attacker-controlled values that matter for the bug enter the library together: `item1` carries the bytes copied into `9.5f`, and `fmtstring` carries the trailing `"{:.0e}"` bytes. Every later vulnerability-relevant transformation is downstream of this call.

coarse_trace.summary: The witness selector byte chooses the `float` specialization and a one-byte argument name, then the harness copies `9.5f` from the fixed data slot and materializes the remaining bytes as the format string `"{:.0e}"`.

Formatting that float with `"{:.0e}"` selects exponential formatting, turns the requested precision into one significant digit, marks the value as binary32, and routes the value into `format_float()`.

The saved crash reaches the fallback formatter, where rounding `9.5` to one significant digit overflows the leading digit and the vulnerable carry-repair code stores `'0'` instead of `'1'` while incrementing the exponent.
Because the malformed leading digit is `'0'`, the later trailing-zero cleanup removes the only stored digit and leaves the stack `memory_buffer` with `size() == 0`.
Exponential prettification still assumes at least one digit, builds the invalid range `digits_ + 1 .. digits_ + 0`, and `copy_str()` overreads the stack buffer while copying from that reversed range.

fine_trace.note: Harness-only dispatch step, not the scored source. The witness byte `0x1a` makes `first == 10`, so the switch selects the `float` instantiation, and `second == 1`, so `invoke_fmt<float>` later treats exactly one byte as the argument name before building the format string.

Source. `invoke_fmt<float>` copies the first four post-selector data bytes into a `float`. For the staged witness those bytes are `00 00 18 41`, yielding `item1 = 9.5f`, the exact tie-rounding input that later overflows the leading digit in `fallback_format()`.

After `invoke_fmt` skips the 16-byte fixed slot and the one-byte argument name selected in step 1, it materializes the remaining six bytes as the format string `"{:.0e}"`. That string is what later requests one significant digit in exponential notation.
This call forwards the attacker-controlled format string and the materialized `9.5f` value into fmt's float-formatting path. The saved ASan stack returns to this exact call site in frame 19.

From the parsed `"{:.0e}"` specs, `write<float>` selects `float_format::exp` with `showpoint == false`, turns the requested precision `0` into one significant digit, and marks the value as `binary32` because the active template instantiation is `float`. Those exact parameters drive the later one-digit carry case in `fallback_format()`.

The crash-reproducing witness reaches the fallback formatter through this error branch. That is the only path to the patched carry site, and the patch's added regression test uses the same `9.5` / `"{:.0e}"` combination.

With one requested significant digit for `9.5f`, the last generated digit is `9` and the round-half-to-even test requests a carry because the tie lands on an odd digit. The fallback formatter therefore stores the overflow sentinel in the only digit slot.

Root cause. Because `num_digits == 1`, the carry-propagation loop has no earlier digit to repair. When the leading slot still holds the overflow sentinel, the code increments the exponent but writes `'0'` back into the only stored digit instead of `'1'`.

The malformed leading digit from step 8 now looks like an ordinary removable trailing zero. Because this is non-fixed formatting with `showpoint == false`, the cleanup loop strips that only digit, increments the exponent once more, and resizes the stack digit buffer to length 0.

The corrupted intermediate state is propagated into `float_writer`: `digits_` points at the stack `memory_buffer` storage from `write<float>`, but `num_digits_` is now `0` while the format is still exponential.

The exponential-format branch assumes there is at least one digit. With `num_digits_ == 0`, it still dereferences `*digits_` and then constructs the reversed source range `digits_ + 1 .. digits_ + 0`, so `begin` already points one byte past `end` before `copy_str()` starts copying.

Sink. `std::copy` consumes the invalid range from step 11, so the source iterator keeps advancing forward through the stack `memory_buffer` digits storage until ASan reports the first byte past the object. The saved trace shows that trap in `buffer<char>::push_back(char const&)` at `include/fmt/core.h:729` while copying this range.

allocation_context.note: AddressSanitizer identifies local stack object `buffer` in this frame as occupying `[192,728)`, and the invalid read occurs at offset `728`, i.e. one byte past that object.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The root-cause carry bug corrupts the same stack `memory_buffer buffer` digits object that ASan later reports as the overread source in `write<float>`.

poc.trigger: The staged 24-byte witness starts with selector byte `0x1a`, so the harness chooses `float` and `argsize = 1`. The first four data bytes materialize `9.5f`, the one-byte argument name is `0x20`, and the trailing six bytes are exactly `"{:.0e}"`. That exact combination makes fmt request one significant digit in exponential format for `9.5f`, reaches the vulnerable carry case in `fallback_format()`, strips the malformed `'0'` digit back down to zero digits, and then overreads the stack digit buffer in `copy_str()`.

format.name: raw fuzzer_named_arg input
format.contract: A `fuzzer_named_arg` input whose selector byte is exactly `0x1a`, whose first four post-selector bytes are little-endian IEEE754 `9.5f` (`00 00 18 41`), whose next twelve fixed-slot bytes are ignored by the `float` branch, whose one-byte argument name is `0x20`, and whose remaining bytes are exactly `"{:.0e}"`. Those exact semantics make `write<float>` round `9.5f` to one exponential digit, hit the carry-overflow bug in `fallback_format()`, and leave `num_digits_ == 0` before `copy_str()` consumes the invalid range.
